strengths: The virtual-correspondence construction is an original, practically useful approach to difficult three-view pose problems. Combining triangle centroids with existing five-/six-point and P3P solvers substantially simplifies implementation. The calibrated-camera contribution provides a convincing basis for weak acceptance independently of the less successful extensions.

The calibrated results demonstrate useful speed–accuracy trade-offs. In Table 2, 4p3v(M±δ)+R+F achieves PhotoTourism AUC@10 of 70.47 at 75.78 ms, versus 70.54 at 105.50 ms for 5pt+P3P and 66.63 at 76.45 ms for the HC solver. This supports practical value without requiring uniform benchmark dominance.

Evaluation is substantial: 5,000 triplets per scene across PhotoTourism and Cambridge Landmarks, two RANSAC frameworks, fixed-iteration speed–accuracy curves, noise and outlier experiments, and component ablations. The supplementary metric covering all three camera pairs strengthens the evidence beyond the main two-pair metric.

The manuscript clearly explains the approximate nature of the method and acknowledges scene dependence, limited-overlap failures, and negligible benefits from learning after refinement. Selecting the shift and refinement settings on a held-out scene is sound experimental practice.
weaknesses: The shared-focal-length contribution has substantially weaker support. In Table 3, even the most accurate proposed variant achieves AUC@10 of 53.56 at 259.63 ms, compared with 56.79 at 11.72 ms for 6pt+P3P. The basic mean variant also trails in both accuracy and runtime. Four-correspondence estimation remains valuable, but the reported experiments do not demonstrate a competitive operating regime for this extension, and focal-length estimation error is not reported.

The geometric justification does not characterize when the approximation will produce useful poses. Section 7 bounds epipolar distance by the triangle's maximum centroid-to-vertex distance, which can be large and does not bound pose error. Aggregate barycentric heatmaps support the centroid heuristic but do not quantify failure probability under changing depth variation, baseline, or overlap. The acknowledged low-overlap sensitivity therefore remains an important practical limitation.

The learned component provides little demonstrated practical benefit and has a correctness issue in its description. Table 2 reports essentially identical refined accuracy for L and M, with substantially higher runtime for L. Equation (2) defines a signed residual rather than a nonnegative Sampson loss; minimizing it directly would not encourage zero epipolar error. The actual training objective needs clarification.

The baseline comparison is restricted to matches consistent across all three views, although 5pt+P3P and 6pt+P3P can exploit additional correspondences visible in only two views. Consequently, the experiments do not establish the same advantage when those baselines use their full admissible correspondence pools. The synthetic low-inlier experiments additionally use uniformly distributed outliers, limiting conclusions about structured mismatches.

Reproducibility and reporting need improvement. Code release is promised, while numerical RANSAC inlier thresholds and the precise refinement residual are not specified. Table 9 repeats the M±δ accuracy values for L±δ with nearly identical runtimes, despite Table 10 showing a higher standalone cost for L±δ. These inconsistencies require reconciliation, but they do not by themselves invalidate the supported calibrated mean-based contribution.
